sense: written works, especially as an art

evidence: Cic. Leg. 1.5: abest historia litterīs nostrīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plural of littera, a letter of the alphabet, and so also a letter (epistle), a document, an account book, and learning (litterīs studēre). An adjective or the context makes it literature: Graecae, Latīnae litterae; Graecae dē philosophiā litterae, Greek philosophical literature (Cic. Div. 2.5).

evidence: Cic. de Orat. 2.194: in scrīptīs relictum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: What someone has written: a writer’s works rather than literature at large.

evidence: Quint. 2.1.4: grammaticē, quam in Latīnum trānsferentēs litterātūram vocāvērunt
terms.comment: Common in modern Latin for literature, but classically it is writing in letters (Cic. Part. 26), the alphabet (Tac. A. 11.13), grammar and philology (Quint. 2.1.4) and, late, learning (Tert.): Lewis & Short.

phrases.latin: Doctrīnā Graecia nōs et omnī litterārum genere superābat
phrases.english: In learning and in every kind of literature Greece surpassed us
history is missing from our literature

sources: Lewis & Short: littera · Lewis & Short: scribo · Lewis & Short: litteratura
